hypothesis: Which profilers work inside the P1 Lambda (python3.12, arm64, 10,240 MB, SnapStart) and what each costs. Each profiler arm runs P1's code with one profiler on; its cost is the difference in Lambda's own REPORT numbers against a REPORT-only control, paired by round (and by request for warm), Graviton3 only. 'nvidia-spi' (the operator's word) is read as NVIDIA's tooling: nvidia-smi and Nsight Systems/Compute.

conclusion: Applicability (in Lambda): NVIDIA tools (nvidia-smi, nsys, ncu) are INAPPLICABLE because there is no GPU (no /dev/nvidia*, no PCI 0x10de, no driver or libraries; 7 environments, all Graviton3 0xd40). perf, eBPF, ptrace and py-spy --native are DENIED (EPERM; CapEff 0, seccomp filter, perf_event_paranoid 2, no PMU). These WORK: P1 phase timers, REPORT/CloudWatch, X-Ray, the Telemetry API extension, cProfile, py-spy --nonblocking, and an in-process SIGPROF sampler (lkaisamp), which gives native KleidiAI kernel profiles where perf is denied. Overhead vs REPORT-only (mean of 5 per-round paired deltas, Graviton3): phase timers and X-Ray not measurable. cProfile +107 ms Init (13%). Telemetry extension +98 ms Init (12%). py-spy +4.8% per warm request (>0 in 25/25 cells) and +24 ms on the first restored request. lkaisamp +0.9% warm (noise) but +377 ms cold and +2.1 s first-after-restore Duration; the delta is outside the baseline's internal timing but occurs before `lkai_prof.handler` returns, and attribution within its dump/symbolise hook remains open. Final latency comparisons should use REPORT or phase timers only. Hot spots: cold = S3 download 25.0 s (69.5%, TLS reads) then the KleidiAI repack 8.4 s (23.4%; buffer_set_tensor + rhs_pack, single-threaded offline). Restore = Lambda restore 3.30 s (83%), then a first forward 2.8x warm whose time is 50% memset inside llama_kv_cache::clear / llama_memory_recurrent::clear. Warm = KleidiAI i8mm matmul 50% of CPU, then f32 dot 8%, gated-delta-net 8%, OpenMP barrier 6%, concat 5%, fwht 5%. Platform finding: the first restore wave of every round (5/5) after publishing 7 versions back to back had 9 of 10 invokes never start (no RESTORE_START, no throttle); cause not established. Status is inconclusive because this is a measurement study, not a latency change.

lkai-p3-cprofile: Python 3.12's cProfile runs on sys.monitoring, process-wide, so one profile sees the import thread, PR #77's load thread and the 32 download threads. Two concurrent profiles are refused ("Another profiling tool is already active", a first deploy failed init with Runtime.ExitError on exactly this). No native frames.

py-spy 0.4.2 static aarch64 binary shipped in the zip, run as the function's own child: `dump --nonblocking` of the parent works (process_vm_readv of the parent is allowed for a child), `record --nonblocking` records in lkai-p3-pyspy

`py-spy dump --native` and `dump` without --nonblocking of a child: "Failed to suspend process ... EPERM: Operation not permitted" (lambda-probe/q1.json -> py_spy.dump_child_native / dump_child_blocking). Suspending needs ptrace: PTRACE_SEIZE and PTRACE_ATTACH of our own child both EPERM. PR_SET_PTRACER is also EPERM.
rows.offline: works on the Graviton host (graviton/pyspy-native.txt) and costs about +29% per forward there (overhead_vs_plain.pyspy)

rows.evidence: perf_event_open of a user-space-only hardware cycles counter, software cpu-clock and software task-clock on the calling thread: all EPERM in every environment (lambda-probe -> syscalls.perf_event_open), with perf_event_paranoid 2, no PMU devices and CapEff 0. perf is also not in the runtime image.
rows.offline: works on the Graviton DevSpace (paranoid 2, armv8_pmuv3_0 PMU): perf stat, perf record -F 999 -g, graviton/perf-*

rows.evidence: bpf(BPF_MAP_CREATE, array) EPERM; unprivileged_bpf_disabled=1; /sys/fs/bpf, tracefs and debugfs absent; no CAP_BPF/CAP_SYS_ADMIN

rows.tool: ptrace-based tools (gdb, strace, ltrace, async stack dumpers)
rows.evidence: PTRACE_SEIZE and PTRACE_ATTACH on a child the probe started: EPERM; no gdb/strace/ltrace on PATH

setitimer(ITIMER_PROF) SIGPROF is delivered (19 signals in 0.2 s CPU, lambda-probe -> itimer_prof_sigprof). lkai-p3-sampler records the interrupted PC and LR of whichever thread is on CPU, tagged by phase, and symbolises in the function from /proc/self/maps and the ELF .symtab/.dynsym of the shipped libraries (the shipped ggml/llama libraries keep .symtab: libggml-cpu-armv8.6_1.so, the variant Graviton3 loads, has 2,459 FUNC symbols, 733 of them KleidiAI kai_*). Limits: no stack walk (PC + caller only); one SIGPROF pending per process, so the effective rate per CPU-second is below 1 kHz (reported as effective_hz_per_cpu_s); CPU time only, so waits (S3 reads, futexes) are invisible.
The runtime is python3.12; there is no JVM. Its Python counterparts are py-spy and cProfile above.
